legend: Kwords%%ZSMJ0%% has a permutation a1,a2,...,an%%ZSMJ1%% of 1%%ZSMJ2%% to n%%ZSMJ3%%, now you can ask him no more than 10%%ZSMJ4%% questions to guess the permutation.
For each query, you can give him a set s%%ZSMJ5%% of k(1≤k≤n)%%ZSMJ6%% indexes, he will give you a sorted array of [as1,as2,...,ask]%%ZSMJ7%%.
Kwords%%ZSMJ8%% thinks the problem is very interesting and invites you to solve it with him.
input: The first line contains a single integer n(1≤n≤1000)%%ZSMJ9%%.
output: When you are ready to answer, print a single line of the form "! a1%%ZSMJ10%% a2%%ZSMJ11%% …%%ZSMJ12%% an%%ZSMJ13%%" (1≤ai≤n)%%ZSMJ14%%, where a%%ZSMJ15%% is a permutation.
When you are ready to query, print a single line of the form "k%%ZSMJ16%% s1%%ZSMJ17%% s2%%ZSMJ18%% …%%ZSMJ19%% sk%%ZSMJ20%%" (1≤k,si≤n)%%ZSMJ21%%.
After printing a line, do not forget to flush the output. Otherwise, you will get Idleness limit exceeded. To do this, use:
You will get Wrong answer if you ask more than 10%%ZSMJ22%% questions.
